newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia delays controversial seminar on Sukarno.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia delays controversial seminar on Sukarno.

text.p: Indonesia has decided to delay a controversial seminar on its first president Sukarno until after the May 29 general election, the Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Thursday.

Minister of Youth Affairs and Sport Hayono Isman, who proposed the seminar, told reporters after meeting leaders of the parliament that the seminar would be delayed until the political climate had cooled.
"We think it will be inappropriate to hold the seminar this month as originally planned because everybody will be pre-occupied with the election," Isman was quoted as saying.
"We are afraid that participants will not dare speak their minds," he said.

The seminar, approved by President Suharto last week, was to focus on Sukarno's final public speech made to the provisional People's Consultative Assembly (MPRS) in June 1966 when he denied any links to the abortive September 1965 Communist coup.

Retired general Abdul Haris Nasution, then head of the MPRS, was also quoted as saying on Wednesday that it should be postponed because of the forthcoming poll, for which campaigning starts on April 27.
In approving the seminar, Suharto said it would show he came to power by constitutional means.

Suharto, one of the few senior generals to survive the 1965 coup attempt, took control of the country and subsequently crushed the Communist party. He was given executive power by Sukarno in March 1966 in a letter that was later lost.
The MPRS, whose members were appointed by Suharto, made him acting president in 1967 and confirmed him in the post a year later.
Suharto is expected to be elected unopposed for his seventh five-year term as president in March next year.
